- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days, then plateau or slightly decline — but true prices rise sharply later, suggesting model fails to capture late-stage momentum.
- After a spike in true prices (e.g., 93+), model forecasts remain flat or slightly above, indicating it overestimates the peak and fails to anticipate subsequent pullback or mean reversion.
- Model underreacts to recent high volatility or sharp price increases — e.g., when true prices jump from 80 to 95, forecast doesn’t adjust quickly enough.
- Forecast mean is typically 5–10% below true mean over 30 days — suggests persistent downward bias.
- Model exhibits “lag” behavior: true price spikes often occur 3–5 days after model’s peak, suggesting it’s too slow to react to new information.
- Model tends to overpredict early in the horizon (e.g., first 5 days) and underpredict late (last 5 days), indicating asymmetric error pattern.
- When true prices show strong upward trend, model forecasts lag behind and don’t rise as steeply — suggesting it underestimates upward momentum.
- Model often fails to capture “mean reversion” after sharp spikes — e.g., after 100+ prices, model doesn’t drop back to prior levels, instead stays high or overestimates.
- Model underestimates the “tail” of the price distribution — i.e., it doesn’t account for extreme upward moves in the final 5–10 days.
